subject: Re: Sizing proposal and pricing for Reserved GPU commit — Northbridge AI
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing + pricing recommendation for Northbridge (initial)

Alex — good to meet last week. Based on the workload notes your infra team shared, we sketched three reserved commit options that balance throughput, latency, and unit cost. Attached is a CSV with the request traces you provided (northbridge_workload_profile_v2.csv) and an initial pricing sheet. High-level notes up front:

- Workload profile: variable burst to 2.6k rps for short API calls (avg ctx 512 tokens), stable baseline about 350 rps; chat patterns produce higher KV cache reuse but long-tail contexts up to 4k tokens for a small subset (4%).
- Recommendation: a mixed GPU pool using 8xA100-80GB equivalents for baseline concurrency plus a 2xA100 hot pool for peak burst absorb. This maps to our Reserved Commit SKU: R-8+2.
- Throughput guarantees: we can commit to 99.9% request success under the baseline and provide a burst SLA for up to 30 minutes/day at 120% baseline with the hot pool.
- Pricing: proposed monthly commit in attached sheet; we can offer a 12% volume discount at a 12-month commit and a separate 5% onboarding credit for migration assistance.

Next steps: Ben will follow up with an explicit throughput modeling table (tokens/sec and expected concurrency). Can you confirm whether long-context requests are off the critical path (i.e., can be queued or degraded to a slightly smaller model)? That will materially change the recommended pool size.

Best,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbridge.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Maya Singh <maya.s@northbridge.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing + pricing recommendation for Northbridge (initial)

Thanks, Soojin — that aligns with what we saw. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Long contexts: ~4% of calls hit 3.5–4k tokens and are used for legal-document summaries. Those calls are not latency critical; we can accept slightly higher p95 if it improves cost.
2) Burst profile: the 2.6k rps peak is typically a 10–20 minute window during EMEA morning sync; it's important we avoid rejections during that period.
3) Procurement: we have internal constraints that prefer fixed monthly invoices and prefer to avoid variable overage charges.

Can you confirm whether the R-8+2 SKU would keep p99 under 600ms for typical single-turn generation at 512 tokens? Also, what would the expected monthly committed expense be with the 12% discount?

— Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform, Northbridge AI
alex.chen@northbridge.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing + pricing recommendation for Northbridge (technical modeling)

Alex — quick modeling notes attached (proposed-pricing-sheet.xlsx has the numbers). Short answers:

- p99 latency for 512-token single-turn generation on the baseline R-8 (without hot pool) is ~480–520ms assuming even routing and continuous batching. With the 2x hot pool absorbing bursts, p99 should stay under 600ms during the EMEA peak window. The long-context requests will push p99 for those specific calls to ~1.2–1.6s; since they're non-critical that's acceptable per your note.
- Expected committed expense (list price) for R-8+2: $137,500/month. With a 12-month commit and the 12% volume discount we quoted, net is $121,000/month. Onboarding credit (one-time) would offset the first month by 5% (~$6,075).
- Alternatives: we can reduce baseline to 6 GPUs and keep the 2-hot variant if you want lower fixed cost and accept slightly higher p95 under sustained growth; that'll cut committed cost to ~$104k/mo post-discount.

I can produce a throughput table mapping rps to tokens/sec and expected GPU utilization if helpful.

- Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbridge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.s@northbridge.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing + pricing recommendation for Northbridge (follow-up)

Ben — the numbers look reasonable. Procurement asked whether you can move to fixed monthly billing with a cap on overage at 10% and an annual true-up rather than per-month variable billing. Also, is there room on the 12% discount? We have a competing offer that matches the baseline price but requests a 10-month commit term. If we extend to 24 months with Redwood, can you improve the discount or include reserved capacity credits for the second year?

Maya and I will review the SLA doc you attached and flag any items.

— Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbridge.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing + pricing recommendation for Northbridge (commercials)

Alex — happy to take this one. Pricing flex and contract structure notes:

- Billing: we can do fixed monthly invoices with an annual true-up. We'll include a hard overage cap of 10% so you don't get surprised by variable charges. Overage would be charged at the discounted unit rate.
- Term & discount: for a 24-month commit we can increase the volume discount from 12% to 18%. Alternatively, keep 12% but include a year-2 credit equal to 4% of year-1 spend that can be applied to capacity during year 2. Either path would give you price predictability vs the competitor's 10-month approach.
- Onboarding credit: we can keep the 5% onboarding credit and extend it to include two dedicated migration support days (engineer time) and one extra month of priority support during cutover.
- SLA addendum: we'll add an explicit burst policy that documents the 30-minute/day guarantee and a mechanism for temporary capacity increases (advance notice or auto-detect and bill/prorate).

If this works, I'll have counsel prepare a term sheet and show you the final numbers.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbridge.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing + pricing recommendation for Northbridge (agreement-in-principle)

Marissa — that structure is promising. We prefer the 24-month + 18% discount option but would like the year-2 credit alternative in the contract as a safety valve (i.e., if usage materially undershoots, we can take credits instead of giving back capacity). Please go ahead and circulate a term sheet and SLA addendum. Procurement will prepare a standard PO once we have countersigned terms.

I'll attach an internal spreadsheet with monthly forecast next week. Thanks to the team for the quick turnaround.

— Alex
